metadata.title: Week 5 Progress
metadata.narration_policy: Narration is SCRIPT.md verbatim, one script section per beat: B00 = section 1, B01-B07 = sections 2-8, BOUT = section 9.
metadata.visual_policy: Simple illustrative Manim cards in the humanitarians palette, in the same style as the Week 2 progress video. No photos or recordings of the fellow, no person icons, no real company, product or tool logos. No Duolingo logo, owl or branding: the app is shown only as a generic drawn phone with plain text. Tools named in the narration are generic drawn shapes or plain text. Any file, terminal, browser or video frame shown is drawn, not a screenshot. Every number, meter and ruler is an illustration of what the script says, not real data.
metadata.structure_note: Same simple structure as the Week 2 progress video: Claude composer cold open, seven body cards, logo outro. No hesitant-writer, verdict or Your Turn beats, because the narration is the fellow's script exactly and the script has no lines for them.

portrait_layout.rule: In 9:16, all text and labels sit above 86% of the frame height (y < 0.86 * H), leaving the bottom 14% empty. Portrait text is at least 72 px at 2160x3840. Portrait type is large and labels are short.

metadata.fill_rule: Gate V needs content covering at least 55% of the safe area at 50% and at 85% of every beat. Each scene lays out its full cast early and holds it, and every scene is built to fill the frame.
metadata.library_check: Searched with ./art scenes first: see SHOTLIST.md. Reused: ClaudeComposerAsk / ClaudeComposerAsk916 and LogoOutro / LogoOutro916; B01-B07 are custom Manim.
metadata.reformat: full-length; native portrait graphics; preserve source framing

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Keya, and this is my week five progress update for the Brutalist project, where I'm learning to create videos as code. The voice you're hearing is an AI voice reading my script.

show.event: the ask types in under 'Hi, Keya'
three result lines land: week 5 progress, what I learned, what I noticed
the AI-voice disclosure is spoken while the answered composer holds

props.command: Help me share my week: the video I made, what I learned, and what I noticed.

beats.narration_text: This week's explainer is How Duolingo Decides What You Practice Next. I've been learning Japanese on Duolingo for over a year, so I researched the forgetting curve, spaced repetition, Leitner flashcard boxes, Duolingo's blog posts, and the research paper behind its model.

show.event: title card for the explainer, text only
over a year of Japanese, drawn as a phone and a year bar
five research cards: forgetting curve, spaced repetition, Leitner flashcard boxes, blog posts, research paper

shot.visual_intent: title card for the explainer, text only; over a year of Japanese, drawn as a phone and a year bar; five research cards: forgetting curve, spaced repetition, Leitner flashcard boxes, blog posts, research paper.

beats.narration_text: The biggest lesson came from the paper itself. A summary said the model improved engagement by twelve percent. But the results table showed that number compared two versions of the same model. Against the older method, the results were mixed. So I took the number out. Now I check what a number is compared against, not just the headline.

show.event: a summary card says 12% better engagement
the results table: that 12% compares two versions of the same model
against the older method the results are mixed
the number is taken out
the habit: check what a number is compared against

shot.visual_intent: a summary card says 12% better engagement; the results table: that 12% compares two versions of the same model; against the older method the results are mixed; the number is taken out; the habit: check what a number is compared against.

beats.narration_text: I also learned how different a vertical video is from a landscape one. The narration is the same, but a squeezed landscape layout doesn't work on a phone. Each vertical scene needs its own design: one idea at a time, stacked top to bottom, with bigger text.

show.event: the same narration, two frames
a squeezed landscape layout fails on a phone
each vertical scene gets its own design: one idea at a time, stacked top to bottom
bigger text

shot.visual_intent: the same narration, two frames; a squeezed landscape layout fails on a phone; each vertical scene gets its own design: one idea at a time, stacked top to bottom; bigger text.

beats.narration_text: The build also taught me to ask for measurements. Claude Code first gave me a wrong figure for the vertical text size, so I asked it to measure the real frames. Every scene's text was above my seventy-two pixel rule.

show.event: a ruler: ask for measurements
a terminal with a crossed-out figure for the vertical text size
a ruler on a real frame
every scene's text sits above the dashed 72 px rule

shot.visual_intent: a ruler: ask for measurements; a terminal with a crossed-out figure for the vertical text size; a ruler on a real frame; every scene's text sits above the dashed 72 px rule.

beats.narration_text: Some things only a person catches. I picked how to say shimasu, mimasu and Leitner by ear, from test clips. And while watching the previews, I noticed the typing and the voice were out of sync in one scene, and got it fixed.

show.event: three words picked by ear from test clips: shimasu, mimasu, Leitner
typing and voice out of sync in one scene
brought back into sync

shot.visual_intent: three words picked by ear from test clips: shimasu, mimasu, Leitner; typing and voice out of sync in one scene; brought back into sync.

beats.narration_text: I also kept watching Brutalist videos, and looked at what topics other fellows cover, so I could find topics that are my own.

show.event: Brutalist videos being watched
topics other fellows cover
one topic that is my own

shot.visual_intent: Brutalist videos being watched; topics other fellows cover; one topic that is my own.

beats.narration_text: This week, the details mattered: a number needs its comparison, a vertical video needs its own layout, and a claim needs a measurement.

show.event: three takeaway cards: a number needs its comparison, a vertical video needs its own layout, a claim needs a measurement

shot.visual_intent: three takeaway cards: a number needs its comparison, a vertical video needs its own layout, a claim needs a measurement.
